title: Bhavya's Homepage
text: Today we went on a trip to Pondicherry and also had a bit of a debate about some religious issues. I believe the ideal of God is the mother of all ideals. Everybody follows some philosophy, and that might not be explicitly following a written philosophy. However, some things can be established with reasonable rigor, and a lack of knowledge of them causes many difficulties when trying to put things into practice. Today, for unknown reasons, I felt a profound sense of respect for this life for just existing here. Now, the ancient wisdom holds that this existence is bondage. We are in the material world, they say, having pain and blah blah. I do not know what or why I feel this, but perhaps it is some deep intuition that has given me a curious purpose. We abuse so many of these subtle things. Rather than looking at them as tools of bondage, we should look at them as the means of liberation of the soul. Hence, they should be respected, not disregarded, or something; they have their own purpose, which is best fulfilled when they are used in the right manner.

title: Learning Math: What does that mean?
text:
I do math “part-time”, if I may phrase it like that, and having talked to some of my friends who do math “full-time”, I figured out that for them what it means to learn a topic seems very different from what it would mean for me.
So for example, there are these things called modules and a corresponding “theory” called Module Theory (just like Ring Theory or Field Theory or … Number Theory?). Now all that came to my mind when we were talking about modules was their definition and perhaps the fact that we can import some tools from linear algebra (although recall that vector spaces are over fields). Now, I have not yet taken a proper course on the topic (as is the case with most of my mathematical knowledge) so there might be a skill issue.
There was a similar conversation with somebody another day and it will take time for me to remember the precise details but if we go on vibes, then I was again thinking of something very general – a structure – and maybe some of its abstract properties blah blah. So this vague sense is what I think when you ask me about module theory, blah blah.
Now let us see what the full-timers have to say about this. They are like “now you have to study different kinds of modules; for instance, there are projective modules, …” – they do not think that fundamentally to decide whether they have covered some topic. It is more like once they have studied the most general definition then they have this special phase where they learn about “particular general examples”, if I may say so.
To give a simple analogy, if you ask me about natural numbers, say, I will be thinking of induction, well-ordering, successor, divisibility, factorization, … first while they would talk of even numbers, odd numbers, prime numbers, composite numbers, … first. What might be the reason behind these differences?
One that I can think of is that since I am a part-timer, I do not remember all the nitty-gritty details; I tend to remember the most general things only. On the other hand, they are working with the subject on much finer scales, so the details matter immensely for them I suppose?

Dr Strange represents the Buchi automata (NBA) and he is bargaining with Dormammu (infinite words over \(\Sigma\), i.e., \(\Sigma^\omega\)). The acceptance criterion of an NBA is that on “running” the infinite word through the automata in a non-deterministic fashion, accepting states must be visited infinitely many times during the entire run. This is similar to what Dr Strange does in the movie: he repeatedly revives himself using the time stone visiting the state “Dormammu, I have come to bargain” infinitely often.

title: The No-Friends Hypothesis
text:
More than a decade ago I had heard of this “saying”,

Friends for 7 years, Friends for Life.

Googling this fact we have Gemini output the following explanation (fragment):

Research in sociology and psychology … friendships that survive the seven-year mark far more likely to last a lifetime. … seven-year period includes major life milestones and challenges, maintaining the bond proves … built on deep trust, mutual growth, and consistent connection. Sociologist Gerald Mollenhorst’s research … we tend to lose about half of our close social network every seven years due to life changes. Friendships that make it past … usually those that intentionally adapt to these shifts, … circumstantial connections into permanent family-like bonds. However, … Reddit, long-term friendships are not entirely automatic … strong predictor of a lifelong friendship, but individuals in these forums note that maintaining requires consistent … intentional communication, as people can still naturally grow apart over time.

Quite loving, no? Well if nothing else, then I can at least be sure that not all my memories are fake. Actually this is not true. I had a friend for 7 years in primary school. He stayed friend no more. As usual, the Redittors have lived up to their reputation (which is why they are the primary source of training LLMs nowadays) and their reasoning applies to my case – we stopped talking.
Now people are in general, bluntly speaking, afraid to talk to me. There is this notion of a “class” or whatever. All the people close to me endorse this notion. Make friends of the same class they say. What is this class? Well, it is a notion known to you all from “common sense”. As an example, you see these groups of people at coaching classes. Some are among the smartest people out there and some are randos forced into engineering. They won’t typically be friends. Why not? Well, they are from different classes is one explanation people would give you.
Now you might ask me what do I have to say on this topic of class (or class of topics?) and I remember an experience from my math olympiad days. There are those people who get into the team and others who work with them – the heart of the system if I may say. You message one of them with high expectation, blushing, eagering waiting for your reply. You get none (at least in my experiences). Then you blame them, think of them as evil. There is an abstract separation that you perceive. You might as well think that these people do not grade everybody equally and so on. There is some distrust.
So in my 7riend’s case, he thought me a different class “now” I suppose. So people think. At least the ones who do, and they are afraid. I can Assure you, however, with a capital “A” that my notion of a class is not based on results or achievements. The thing that moves me at the core is effort. I care not whether you top your class. It matters more whether you do your best. I care not whether you can speak or frame sentences flawlessly. It matters more whether you mean what you say.
Now on the topic of friends, I think I have found a universal truth for my case, which is that I am divinely forbidden from having friends. Yeah, I must be an irrational man or whatever. Well but you see, neither the duration of friendship matters, nor the strength. Neither the age matters nor the sex. Year after year they tend to change their names and form. All come after power or pleasure or support and so on. And you see, neither matters whether I wish them their birthday because when you wish them not, they come to you to tell thyself that today is their birthday and you are invited yet when you do wish them, receive an invite you do not. No, the amount of interaction does not matter because when you pour all your love onto them as milk is poured on the Shivling they run away in terror, while when you do not do so friendliness stays intact. But when there is no interaction, some of them fade away like castles made of sand.
Year after year I find moments when I am alone with increasing concentration. Earlier shout in silence I would, now I do not. For they say to see the sun of which all of us are the rays, aloneness is a necessity and so what we have here is a blessing (in disguise).
